entities.name: PMID:25451444
observations: In 50 recent suicide attempters with bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder versus 36 mood-disorder patients without lifetime attempts, serum triglycerides were significantly decreased after adjustment for BMI and waist circumference; total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, and leptin did not differ.

entities.name: PMID:24495778
observations: In 555 adults with major depressive disorder, recent suicide attempters had lower triglycerides and higher HDL; triglycerides were negatively associated with current suicidality (β = −0.187, p = 0.039), while other lipid profiles generally showed no significant group differences.

entities.name: PMID:19026707
observations: In a small hospitalized male bipolar sample, suicide attempters had lower total cholesterol (p = 0.013) and triglycerides (p = 0.047) than non-attempters.

entities.name: PMID:22230650
observations: In 220 bipolar patients, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and HDL-C did not differ significantly by lifetime suicide-attempt status.

entities.name: PMID:25969160
observations: In 50 bipolar-I patients, cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides did not differ significantly between suicide attempters and non-attempters.

entities.name: PMID:28627446
observations: A meta-analysis of 11 bipolar studies found no pooled difference for total cholesterol (SMD −0.10, 95% CI −0.30 to 0.10, p = 0.34), LDL-C (SMD −0.26, 95% CI −0.65 to 0.13, p = 0.19), or triglycerides (SMD −0.06, 95% CI −0.31 to 0.19, p = 0.63).

entities.name: PMID:20712167
observations: In 26 medically serious suicide attempters with bipolar disorder or major depressive disorder versus 87 controls, cholesterol and triglycerides did not differ significantly; cholesterol was nonsignificantly higher and triglycerides nonsignificantly lower in attempters.
